How do I get access to the EHR system?.answer:
To get EHR access, submit an access request to **it@mentella.example** with your full name and regional pod [2]. Include a screenshot of any error message if you encounter one — it helps speed up processing [2].

Here's the key step: your supervisor must countersign your request before your account becomes active [3]. This is a HIPAA requirement ensuring that a named, accountable person authorizes your access to client information [3].

Your supervisor will receive an automatic notification when you submit the form. If you don't see a countersignature within 2 business days, reach out to your supervisor directly or escalate to it@mentella.example [3].

Once you have access, review the HIPAA Do's and Don'ts doc to understand what you're allowed to do [2].

I'm not sure about your first paycheck timing — that's not covered in these excerpts. For that question, please reach out to ops@mentella.example.

For direct deposit, here's what I can tell you: Set it up in your Paylocity profile during your first week [1][2]. You can add up to 3 accounts and split pay by percentage or fixed amount [1]. Keep in mind that changes take one full pay cycle to take effect, so set it up early [1]. Direct deposit is one of three day-1 checklist items alongside tax forms and your emergency contact [1][2].

How do I request time off?.answer:
Here's how to request time off:

**For time off longer than a single day:** Submit your PTO request in Paylocity at least 2 weeks in advance [1]. Before submitting, block those dates in Calendly and cancel or reassign any client sessions already booked during that window [1]. Approval can be delayed if your calendar shows open availability while you're requesting time off [1].

**For personal emergencies:** Same-day or next-day PTO doesn't require the 2-week notice—just notify your pod lead as soon as possible [1].

The key is to manage your calendar *before* you submit the request so there's no conflict between your availability and your time-off dates.

Where is client information allowed to l.answer:
Client information is allowed to live **only in the EHR (Electronic Health Record)** [1][3]. 

PHI—Protected Health Information—may never be created, stored, or discussed in email, Slack, shared spreadsheets, personal notes apps, text messages, or any channel outside the EHR [3]. This applies even when communicating with supervisors or about scheduling.

If you need to flag something about a client to a colleague, use the EHR's internal messaging system instead [3].
